text: An existing Python application's commands run as an explicit Docker user, so Linux Docker can open the gate's private mounts (#399, #412). Those mounts come from os.MkdirTemp, mode 0700 and owned by the gate's user, and on Linux the image's root, with every capability dropped, can't enter them: on GitHub's runners every command failed before it started. Before each command, the executor reads the selected daemon's security options with docker info --format '{{json .SecurityOptions}}'. Ordinary Docker runs the command as the gate's effective host UID:GID. Rootless Docker runs it as 0:0, whose container root maps to the daemon's owner. Discovery that fails or can't be parsed, and rootful user-namespace remapping, refuse before any application container starts, with no fallback, and the directories keep their 0700 permissions. Every other limit is unchanged. TestPythonApplicationGatePrivateMounts runs a real Docker Python and TLC gate in CI's Linux integration shards with no opt-in.
